title: Multi-Hook Linked List Runner
subtopicTitle: Hooks Linked List & Rules of Hooks
concept: Fiber memoizedState Linked List & Sequential Traversal
problemStatement: Implement `createHookRunner()` that supports multiple calls to `useState()` across consecutive render passes, storing them in a linked-list structure and maintaining state continuity.
interviewTrap: React does not use key names for hooks! It relies 100% on execution call order to pair each hook with its corresponding slot in the linked list.

testCases.name: Maintains multiple independent hook states in order
testCases.testFn: const r = createHookRunner(); r.prepareRender(); const [name] = r.useState('Alice'); const [age] = r.useState(25); return [name, age];

testCases.name: Preserves updated values across multiple renders
testCases.input: setState updates state on next render pass
testCases.testFn: const r = createHookRunner(); r.prepareRender(); const [, setName] = r.useState('Alice'); const [, setAge] = r.useState(25); setName('Bob'); setAge(prev => prev + 1); r.prepareRender(); const [name2] = r.useState(); const [age2] = r.useState(); return [name2, age2];

testCases.name: Handles 3 or more hooks in strict sequence
testCases.testFn: const r = createHookRunner(); r.prepareRender(); r.useState(1); r.useState(2); r.useState(3); r.prepareRender(); return [r.useState()[0], r.useState()[0], r.useState()[0]];

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Real React hooks are stored not in a flat array, but as a singly-linked list of Hook nodes on the Fiber: `fiber.memoizedState -> hook1 -> hook2 -> hook3 -> null`. Building a Multi-Hook Linked List Runner illustrates how `useState`, `useReducer`, and `useMemo` share the same linked list structure.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Define Hook node structure: `{ memoizedState, next }`.
During mount (`mountWorkInProgressHook`): instantiate a new Hook node, append to tail of linked list.
Support multiple hook invocations per component in strict sequential order.
Component re-render traverses the existing linked list node-by-node.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In `ReactFiberHooks.js`, `currentlyRenderingFiber` keeps track of the active fiber. Both `mount` and `update` phases execute different dispatchers: `HooksDispatcherOnMount` creates the nodes, while `HooksDispatcherOnUpdate` reads and updates existing nodes in the linked list.

complexity.time: O(1) access per hook call during render traversal.
complexity.space: O(H) nodes where H is count of hooks.

edgeCasesHandled: Multiple hooks of different types (state, memo, reducer) coexist on same linked list.
Preserves correct individual hook state across multiple re-render passes.
Reaching end of linked list properly matches expected hook count.

specifications: React Architecture Docs: Hooks Linked List Representation
verifiedRules: Fiber.memoizedState stores the head of the hook linked list.
Every hook node has a .next pointer pointing to the next hook.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How are different hook types (useState, useMemo, useEffect) stored on the same fiber.memoizedState?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: All hooks share the exact same `Hook` node struct: `{ memoizedState, baseState, baseQueue, queue, next }`. What differs is what `memoizedState` holds: for `useState`, it holds the state value; for `useMemo`, it holds `[cachedValue, deps]`; for `useEffect`, it holds the `Effect` ring buffer node; for `useRef`, it holds `{ current: val }`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests architectural understanding of hook node polymorphism.

realWorldUseCases.scenario: Multi-Hook State Container in React Reconciler
realWorldUseCases.description: Components combining useState, useMemo, and useRef on a shared singly-linked list.

howToExplain.opening: Hooks are stored as a homogeneous singly-linked list on fiber.memoizedState, where each node's memoizedState property holds hook-specific payloads.
keyPoints: useState stores values; useMemo stores [value, deps]; useRef stores { current }.
workInProgressHook cursor steps through nodes in invocation order.
Mount phase creates nodes; update phase reads and reuses existing nodes.
howToExplain.closingImpression: This unified linked list structure is why all hooks obey the exact same ordering rules.
analogies: Train boxcars: all cars have the same couplers (.next), but car 1 carries coal (state), car 2 carries grain (memo), and car 3 carries tools (ref).

commonMistakes.mistake: Thinking useRef triggers re-renders when mutated.
commonMistakes.why: useRef simply returns a persistent object { current: value }. Mutating .current does not schedule any fiber updates.
commonMistakes.correct: Clarify that useRef provides mutable storage without triggering renders.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does React manage the update queue on a useState hook?
followUpDeepDive.answer: `hook.queue.pending` is a circular singly-linked list of update actions. Using a circular list allows React to keep pointers to both the head (for fast traversal) and the tail (for O(1) appends) with a single pointer.
